dataAvailability.evidence: No structured, re-fetchable, deterministic occupation/employer field exists anywhere in this repo's schema or ingest pipeline — confirmed at three levels: (1) the PSP open-data osoby.unl bulk dump this repo actually ingests has no such column, (2) the person node's prop catalogue in graph-schema.md has no occupation-class prop, (3) a live fetch of psp.cz's own MP detail page for Josef Kott (the case that motivated this probe) shows no occupation/employer field either — confirming the psp.cz bio page itself does not expose it, so there is no missed ingest opportunity there. The ONLY place employer/occupation-adjacent facts appear in this repo is inside effort_public_role / effort_notes free text, written by prior Sonnet dossier passes (batches 001-003) doing ad hoc open-web research per MP — present for 29 of 85 dossiered MPs (34%), absent for the other 122 of 207 MPs who have no dossier yet at all. This text is real and usable for keyword mining, but it is not a structured field, has no citation/provenance for the employer claim itself, and its presence is an accident of what each dossier-writer happened to research, not a systematic sweep.

proposedSignal.name: employment_coi_candidate
proposedSignal.rule: Deterministic (given the input corpus) two-stage filter, NOT a raw-data-level signal — it operates over already-existing LLM-authored effort_public_role + effort_notes text, not over any ingested table: (1) KEYWORD SCAN — regex-match employer/company/profession indicators in Czech (jednatel, ředitel(ka), produktový/obchodní/generální manažer(ka), zaměstnanec/zaměstnankyně, podnikatel(ka), a.s./s.r.o., OSVČ, lékař(ka)/chirurg, and similar role nouns), EXCLUDING public-office titles (starosta/starostka, hejtman, primátor, ministr — these are elected/appointed public roles, not private employment, and must not count as an employer hit). (2) SECTOR CROSS-REFERENCE — map the matched employer's apparent sector (agriculture, health/medicine, defense/security, finance, energy, IT, etc., inferred from the matched company name or profession noun) against the MP's current committee memberships via a fixed committee-abbrev→sector table (ZEV→agriculture, VZ→health, VO→defense, RV/SKFAÚ→finance, VB/KV/SK*BIS/SKNBÚ/SKNÚKIB→security-oversight, etc.). `employment_coi_candidate = true` only when both stages hit: a private-sector employer/professional-tie keyword AND a same-sector current committee seat. Output includes the matched keyword span and committee(s) as `reason`, for human review — this is a candidate flag for the same pending_review gate used by `linked_to` edges, never an auto-published verdict.
inputs: person.committees[] (abbrev + role, from dossier input payloads, not currently a queryable graph-node prop — would need to be added to kg person props to run this at graph scale)
a hand-maintained committee-abbrev → sector keyword map (new, not yet in the repo)
a hand-maintained public-office exclusion list (starosta, hejtman, primátor, ministr, náměstek, radní, zastupitel — to avoid conflating elected local office with private employment)
falsePositiveRisks: Expected professional overlap is not conflict: a physician on the Health Committee (Šrámková, pspId 7046) or a surgeon on the Health Committee is normal domain expertise, not a Kott-style conflict — the signal cannot distinguish 'MP with relevant expertise self-selected onto the fitting committee' from 'MP still financially tied to a company regulated/funded via that committee' without knowing whether the employment is CURRENT and whether money still flows.

Stale/historical employment: text sometimes explicitly states a role ended years ago (e.g. pspId 5226: 'zakládající ředitel ÚSTR 2006-2010, dnes bez výkonné role') — a naive keyword hit would still fire on committee overlap even though the tie is defunct; the rule needs (but free text doesn't reliably supply) a recency field.

Sector inference from a company name is fuzzy and can mismatch (e.g. is a 'winery' agriculture or food-industry? is 'ACT CZ, IT + betting shops' security-adjacent or not?) — the sector map will need ongoing hand-tuning and will both over- and under-match at the margins.

Coverage bias, not absence of conflict: only 85/207 MPs (41%) have any dossier text at all, and within those, employer mentions are present for only 29 (34% of 85, 14% of 207) — a MP with NO fire is not evidence of no conflict, it is very likely evidence nobody researched their employer yet. Reporting 'did not fire' must not be read as 'clear'.

The underlying employer claim itself carries no citation/provenance in the current text — 'podle veřejných zdrojů' / 'dle dobového tisku' is not a re-verifiable source, so any candidate this signal surfaces needs a fresh, cited web-research pass before being treated as more than a lead.
Public-office exclusion list is hand-maintained and incomplete by construction — any elected-office title not on the list would false-positive as a 'company'.

(Agrofert group) + current committees ZEV (Zemědělský výbor / agriculture, member) and KV (Kontrolní výbor / control, vice-chair) — sector match on agriculture, plus the oversight-role angle from the original case. recommendation: Defer, do not ship as an auto-flag. There is no structured, re-fetchable occupation/employer field anywhere in this repo or in the PSP open-data dump it ingests — confirmed directly against Kott's own live psp.cz profile, which shows no such field either, so this is not a missed ingest opportunity, it is a genuine absence of the underlying data short of a paid Hlídač Státu token or a bespoke new scrape (e.g. of election-candidacy 'povolání' declarations on volby.cz, which this repo does not currently touch at all). What DOES work, and what the probe demonstrates concretely, is a downstream keyword+committee-sector mining pass over the free-text effort_public_role/effort_notes already produced by prior dossier batches: run against 16 MPs it correctly re-derived the seed Kott case and surfaced three more plausible non-Kott candidates (Teleky, Krutáková, Němečková Crkvenjaš) while correctly declining to fire on a same-committee coincidence with a non-matching employer (Macinka) and on public-office holders (Bačíková, Vlček, Okleštěk). But it also produced a clean textbook false positive (Šrámková, a physician on the Health Committee) and is only run over the 41% of MPs that have dossier text at all, with employer mentions present for barely a third of those — so 'did not fire' cannot be read as 'clear.' Recommendation: land this as a new gated verdict-track lens (same pending_review discipline as `linked_to` money edges), scoped explicitly to the MPs it already fired on plus a widening of dossier coverage past 85/207, rather than as a blind deterministic prop on all 207 person nodes; and treat the recency gap (Krutáková's 'bývalá', Macinka's 2013-2025 institute role) as a required follow-up field before any candidate here is treated as more than a lead worth a human's five minutes.
